news.title: England aim to win over Wembley and revive Wonderwall in Spain glamour fixture
news.lede: Emotions of a Nations League match cannot pulse to the same levels as the World Cup but Tuchel needs to reconnect. Thomas Tuchel has pictured the scene. It comes after the final whistle has blown on England’s Nations League opener against Spain on Saturday night, the first post-World Cup fixture for both teams, and it has Wembley swaying to the strains of Wonderwall. It is a moment of communion, a reconnection with the Oasis classic that was the soundtrack to England’s World Cup campaign, which delivered so much only to end in such disappointment.

news.title: This college football team adopted Norway's Viking Row — here's who is keeping the World Cup chant alive
news.lede: Norway's Viking Row was one of the most viral fan traditions of the 2026 World Cup. Now, months later, the chant has officially made its way onto American college football fields. The University of Minnesota debuted its own version of the synchronized rowing chant at its season opener at Huntington Bank Stadium. In the stands, the student section sat shoulder-to-shoulder in rows, pulling imaginary oars in unison and mimicking the exaggerated motion Norwegian supporters made famous this past summer.

news.title: New-look Brazil set for post-World Cup reset
news.lede: Carlo Ancelotti's Brazil and hosts Australia will use their friendly double-header as the first stage of a rebuilding process following the World Cup. Brazil take on the Socceroos in Townsville today (4:00pm Bangladesh Time) before a second clash in Brisbane next Tuesday. It will be both countries' first outings since their World Cup campaigns ended in July. The Socceroos bowed out in the round of 32 while five-time champions Brazil suffered a shock loss to Norway in the last 16.

news.title: Bonus for the World Cup: Spain star gives up one million euros to federation employees
news.lede: A press report revealed today, Thursday, a stunning surprise concerning one of the players of the Spain national team, crowned champions of the 2026 World Cup. Money isn't always everything in football, according to newspaper "AS", and it pointed to a fresh example: someone who will wear two stars on his chest this Saturday at Wembley Stadium, where Spain face England in the UEFA Nations League. The player in question, whose identity the paper did not reveal, gave up his World Cup winning bonus and donated it to the staff of the Spanish Football Federation in appreciation of their outstanding efforts.
